transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-12-15
Time: 14:30 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Daniel (Redwood SE), Aisha (Zephyr Head of Search), Tom (Zephyr ML), Priya (Zephyr PM)
---
Summary (auto): quick demo of embeddings + rerank; pilot & benchmarks requested; security follow-up.

00:00 Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood, AE on the account. Daniel our SE will walk through the embeddings + rerank flow. Aisha, thanks for taking time.
00:08 Aisha: Yeah thanks, excited to see how this could improve our relevancy, we've been experimenting with hybrid BM25 + embeddings, but reranking has been a pain at scale.
00:20 Daniel: Great. I'll start with a quick architecture overview and then do a live API demo - we'll show the embeddings endpoint, how we store vectors, and then the rerank endpoint that takes candidate doc ids + query and returns re-ranked results.
00:33 Tom: Quick question before you start - are you showing hosted only or also dedicated/private? Our infra folks will want to know we can run this in VPC later.
00:40 Maya: Today is hosted demo; we will cover Dedicated/Private in the follow-up security call. For now, hosted has optional VPC peering and KMS integration; we'll share the security doc.
00:52 Daniel: ok jumping in - here's the minimal flow: 1) call /embeddings to vectorize the query and docs, 2) store vectors in your vector DB or Redwood managed index, 3) at query time run a fast ANN to get candidates then call /rerank with the top N candidates and the original query.
01:06 Daniel: I'll paste a sample curl - note the embeddings endpoint uses model param, size; returns a 1,024-d float vector in our example. (screen share)
01:20 Aisha: Are embeddings returned normalized? We tried cosine in-house.
01:23 Daniel: Good Q - we provide raw float vectors; we recommend L2-normalize on your side or use the reranker with cosine-based scoring. Our SDKs include helpers to normalize.
01:36 Priya: For reranking latency, what's realistic at 100 qps and top-50 candidates?
01:40 Daniel: For hosted, typical p95 for rerank with a 7B reranker is ~90-150ms depending on sequence length - for top-50 candidates we see higher token counts. We also have batching and prefix cache that can reduce cost; if you need strict SLOs Dedicated gives you more predictable tails.
01:58 Tom: That 90-150ms is for the reranker compute only or includes ANN?
02:02 Daniel: That's compute only - ANN time varies by your index, but with a managed index we keep ANN under 30ms for moderate sized corpora. If you want end-to-end numbers we can run a 5k query benchmark with your data.
02:17 Maya: we'll do that as part of the pilot. Daniel, note they'll want the sheet with latency, cost per query, and recall vs old system.
02:25 Daniel: noted. I'll run the benchmark and upload spreadsheet - link will be provided.
02:31 Aisha: On security - we need SOC 2 + not sending PII to third parties. How's data retention and encryption?
02:38 Maya: Hosted supports optional ephemeral retention and can be configured to not persist inputs; we also integrate with customer KMS for encryption at rest, and audit logs are available via the console. I'll attach the security pack after the call.
02:50 Priya: Also, can we limit model choices and prevent model upgrades automatically? We can't let a different model roll out mid-pilot.
02:56 Daniel: Yes, you can pin model versions per route in the Console and the API accepts model version param. Rollouts are manual or can be scheduled - we support canary and automatic fallback to a pinned variant.
03:08 Daniel: Alright switching to a short live demo - here's a Jupyter snippet hitting /embeddings. I'm using the hosted API key, and you'll see I pass model=text-embed-4xz (example), we get back vector length 1024.
03:30 (typing, brief pause)
03:45 Daniel: Now I'll show the rerank call - we pass query plus an array of candidate documents (id, text, metadata). The rerank endpoint returns a score and optionally a normalized_rank field.
04:00 Aisha: Are there rate limits or quotas that will affect us during pilot? We have spikes from user testing.
04:06 Maya: We have quotas by default but can open bursts for pilots; for production we can set committed throughput on Dedicated. For hosted we can temporarily increase quota for benchmarking.
04:18 Tom: For large docs we sometimes hit token limits; how do you handle chunking / long contexts?
04:23 Daniel: We recommend chunking and embedding chunks; reranker handles concatenated snippets but for very long doc lists we use a two-stage approach - ANN on chunk embeddings then rerank concatenated top-k snippets. Our Console has a chunking policy UI to tune snippet size.
04:40 Priya: Is there built-in monitoring to see per-route token cost and latency?
04:45 Maya: Yes the Console shows per-route token and latency breakdown, token-level cost estimates, and model-level dashboards. You can hook tracing to your own telemetry.
04:54 Aisha: Could you highlight Optimize suggestions? We heard you have batching/caching suggestions.
05:00 Daniel: Yup. Redwood Optimize inspects traffic patterns and suggests batching window sizes, cache TTLs for prefix caching, and quantization profiles for reranker models to cut cost. For example, switching a reranker to 4-bit quantization reduced tokens/second cost by ~35% in our internal tests with small latency impact.
05:20 Tom: Would quantization be available on hosted?
05:22 Daniel: Yes, we run quantized variants and will fallback if quality regresses. We provide quality gates and eval runs before recommending.
05:30 Priya: For ranking metrics - precision@k and NDCG - can we surface those in Console or do we need to run our own evals?
05:37 Daniel: Console supports linking to your eval harness; we can also ingest your labeled pairs and show NDCG/P@k trends and quality regression alerts tied to prompts and eval sets.
05:50 (short screen flicker)
06:05 Daniel: I'm going to demo an end-to-end sample: search endpoint returns candidate IDs from an ANN search, then we call /rerank; here's the JSON flow. Note: the transcript may mis-say some parts - the SDK helper function is rerankCandidates().
06:30 Aisha: We're using Elastic as our primary index - is Redwood's managed ANN compatible or do we need to migrate?
06:36 Daniel: You can keep Elastic for document store and use Redwood for embeddings + rerank. We integrate with popular vector DBs or provide a managed index. Migration is optional.
06:50 Tom: About cost - what ballpark for 1M searches/month with top-50 rerank?
06:55 Maya: Rough estimate depends on embedding model and reranker size. We'll provide a pricing example but expect hosted to be higher than Dedicated per qps but no infra ops. We'll run numbers for your profile in the pricing deck.
07:10 Priya: If we start pilot, what's the onboarding time?
07:14 Maya: Typically 1-2 weeks to spin up keys, run sample ingest and a small benchmark. For a 5k-query benchmark we can have initial results in ~1 week.
07:23 Daniel: I'll need a sample dataset CSV with query-candidate pairs and relevance labels for the eval. That helps us produce NDCG and compare to baseline.
07:33 Priya: We'll prepare that.
07:40 Aisha: A few technical nitpicks - how do you handle cold-start model weights and warming? We have bursty traffic in the morning.
07:46 Daniel: The runtime keeps model workers warm for a percentage of capacity depending on your SLO. There's a warm pool and smart routing; some of the language may be transcribed as "KV cash" in older notes but it's KV cache - we use prefix cache to speed repeated prefixes.
08:05 Maya: We'll also add a note: for unpredictable bursts Dedicated is better since you get committed capacity. Hosted can burst but there's a fallback policy.
08:13 Tom: Any limitations around PII/PCI?
08:15 Maya: We have data handling policies, optional non-persistence, and Private deployment if you need air-gapped. Security pack will include SOC2 and encryption details.
08:28 Daniel: Ok last part - I'll show the Console quick workflows. (screen share Console) Here you can create a route that pins model, sets batching window, and sets rerank threshold. You can also view cost by token and per-route latency.
09:00 (Console demo continues, a few clicks)
09:25 Priya: The UI looks straight-forward. Can we set alerts on quality regression?
09:29 Daniel: Yes, tie alerts to eval sets and we can trigger rollback if quality drops below a threshold.
09:38 Aisha: For the pilot, can we start with hosted and then evaluate Dedicated?
09:41 Maya: Absolutely. Pilot on hosted makes sense then we evaluate Dedicated if tails or cost require it.
09:48 Maya: Ok let's recap the concrete next steps so everyone is aligned.
09:52 Maya: Action items - Maya will send pricing + security pack by Friday; Daniel will run a 5k-query rerank benchmark and share results; Zephyr will provide dataset and acceptance criteria. We'll schedule a security deep-dive with infra.
10:08 Aisha: That sounds good, thanks. One last thing - can you share a sample integration repo?
10:12 Daniel: Yes, I'll include a GitHub example with curl, python SDK, and node snippets.
10:18 Priya: Great, thanks everyone.
10:22 Maya: Thanks all, we'll follow up with calendar invites for the security call.
